summary: Converted the test suite's remaining genuinely-flaky sleep-then-assert tests to wait on the condition they actually claim, with a deadline as a deadlock guard rather than a measurement (issue #180).
details: tests/unit/test_runtime.py::test_a_scheduled_watermark_free_adaptor_fires_again_after_the_interval was the suite's only TWO-SIDED count assertion (`2 <= len(calls) < 12`): the lower bound had 3x margin, the upper bound had ZERO — `_slot` buckets on real wall-clock time, not monotonic(), so a stretched `asyncio.sleep` under load can push the count past 12 from the OTHER direction. Now waits on an asyncio.Event set by the second fire and cancels immediately, which makes the old upper bound structural instead of a magic constant. A first attempt also re-proved 'not firing every tick' via `nora_dream_skipped_total{reason="schedule"}` between the two fires; measured over 8 solo reruns it failed 3 times, because whether any tick lands inside the ~20ms window before the slot boundary depends on real-clock phase alignment — reintroducing #180's own failure mode inside its own fix. Dropped in favour of the two sibling tests (fires-once-and-holds; runs-every-tick-with-no-schedule) that already prove it without a clock.

tests/test_main.py::test_the_prune_sweep_actually_prunes slept a fixed 0.1s over a 0.01s sweep interval and asserted the row count directly; observed failing (`assert 10 == 3`) 1 run in 3 under a loaded serial `make gate` against a real Postgres container. Now polls the store until the row count drops, deadline-guarded.

tests/unit/test_debrief.py::test_the_two_calls_start_before_either_finishes dropped its `elapsed < 0.18` perf_counter bound (80ms of slack over two overlapped 0.10s sleeps) — a machine measurement that gets MORE likely to fail under load, not less, and was redundant: the adjacent `events == ["start", "start", "end", "end"]` assertion already proves the real concurrency claim the test's name makes.

tests/unit/test_engagement_pipeline.py: 7 call sites slept a fixed 0.02s to let a spawned turn reach 'admitted, mid-invoke' before queueing more tags behind it, then asserted queue state. Now poll the pipeline's own `_slots.held(...)` (or, for the queued-tag-gets-its-eyes test, the reaction log) via a new local `_wait_for(predicate, timeout_seconds=5.0)` helper — the same idiom already in tests/infra/compute/test_docker_backend.py — instead of a fixed-turn-count `asyncio.sleep(0)` pump in one case and a fixed-window sleep in the rest.
limitations: Re-measured 2026-09-17 against master, not against the issue body's original counts (its named worst offender, test_discord_voice_session.py, no longer exists — restructured into test_voice_*.py — so that section of #180 is void).

tests/infra/compute/test_docker_backend.py and tests/test_logging.py were left alone on inspection: the former is already sub-millisecond poll loops with 10s deadlines (the pattern this fix generalises), and the latter's sleeps are not count/state assertions.

Every converted test was falsified by hand — production fault injected, confirmed red, reverted — rather than merely re-run green; see the PR description for the fault and the failure each one caught.
